text.p: A cholera outbreak in the West African state of Guinea-Bissau has killed 84 people and 8,345 cases have been reported since authorities declared an epidemic in October, the Portuguese news agency Lusa reported on Monday.
Most of the cases registered so far were in Bissau, capital of the former Portuguese colony, Lusa said, quoting a health ministry source.
Health authorities declared the epidemic on October 11 1996.
The previous cholera epidemic in Guinea-Bissau, which lasted from October 1994 to March 1995, killed 290 people.

Cholera, spread by poor hygiene or the contamination of drinking water by sewage, brings on severe diarrhoea and dehydration and kills if not treated quickly. Outbreaks often coincide with the rainy season in West Africa.
The disease is relatively easy to treat but health workers say rehydration fluids and medicines are in short supply.
